{{short description|Bulgarian applied mathematician}}
'''Angela Slavova''' is a Bulgarian applied mathematician. She heads the Department of Mathematical Physics in the Institute of Mathematics of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, and is former chair of the Bulgarian section of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].

==Education==
Slavova graduated from the [[University of Ruse]] with M.S. in [[computer engineering]] in 1986. From 1992 to 1993, she was a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright scholar]] at the [[Florida Institute of Technology]], but returned to Bulgaria to obtain her Ph.D. in [[mathematics]] in 1995 from her alma mater and in 2005 became Doctor of Science at the [[Institute of Mathematics and Informatics]] of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=cmc>{{cite web|url=https://cmc-dresden.org/team/angela-slavova/|title=Angela Slavova|publisher=Chua Memristor Center|accessdate=1 June 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
From 2004 to 2011, Slavova was a head of the Department of Mathematical Physics of the Institute of Mathematics at the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]]. Since 2007, she has been a full professor at the [[Institute of Mathematics and Informatics]] of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]]. Since 2011, she is a head of the Department of Differential Equations and Mathematical Physics at the Institute of Mathematics, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences.<ref name=cmc/>

She chaired the Bulgarian section [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] for 2013–2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-sections-5|title=SIAM Sections|publisher=SIAM|year=2014|accessdate=2020-01-12}}</ref>

==Books==

* ''Cellular neural networks: dynamics and modelling'' (Kluwer, 2003}.<ref>Review of ''Cellular neural networks: dynamics and modelling'', Xingfu Zou (2004), {{MR|1984633}}</ref>
* ''Nonlinear waves: An introduction'' (World Scientific, 2011)<ref>''Nonlinear waves: An introduction'' is listed (but not reviewed) in {{MR|2766555}}</ref>
* ''Nonlinear waves: A geometrical approach'' (World Scientific, 2019).<ref>Review of ''Nonlinear waves: A geometrical approach'', Boris A. Malomed (2019), {{MR|3887605}}</ref>
